signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Repricing
signals.text: AUD/CHF reflects a dominant G10 divergence as AUD leads with an average weekly gain of +1.038% while CHF lags at -0.645%. This 1.683% spread is driven by higher-than-expected Australian CPI which has reopened the door for RBA tightening, contrasting sharply with the SNB's 0.00% hold. AUD/USD has pushed to 0.7172, comfortably above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7075, 0.7006, 0.6961), confirming broad-based strength. The carry profile remains the primary structural tailwind, with AUD/CHF offering a +435bp carry premium, the highest available among G10 crosses. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/CHF; carry advantage and hawk-RBA repricing support further divergence. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold priced but hawkish guidance expected. Risk: VIX breaks above 25, triggering a flight to safety that favors the CHF and forces a carry unwind.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Positioning + Vol + Geopolitical Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY is trading at 159.33, holding near the 160.00 level which remains the critical threshold for potential BoJ/MoF intervention. COT LF net short position in JPY has expanded to -73,641 (pctl 12) as leveraged funds continue to favor the +275bp Fed-BoJ carry trade despite rising verbal warnings. The options market is signaling caution, with 25d risk reversals showing a strong -1.86 put skew, indicating institutional demand for downside protection against the spot trend. High-impact headlines regarding Japan supporting oil pipelines to bypass the Strait of Hormuz layer a specific energy-security risk onto the pair. Trade bias: Neutral/Range USD/JPY; carry support is offset by acute intervention risk at 160.00. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 64% hike priced) — hike bias active. Risk: Confirmed BoJ intervention triggers a disorderly unwind of the crowded speculative short.

signals.title: AUD/USD — COT vs Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD exhibits a significant positioning divergence at the 0.7172 level as retail and institutional flows collide. COT LF net longs have surged to +49,749 (pctl 94, z +1.78), marking a crowded institutional long that is testing the upper decile of its 52-week range. Conversely, retail sentiment is at an extreme 90% short, attempting to fade the rally following the CPI beat. The pair remains in a clear bullish technical posture, holding above all major SMAs with the SMA20 at 0.7075 providing structural support. This setup typically results in a retail capitulation squeeze if price continues to extend higher toward the 0.7200 psychological barrier. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; retail extreme short provides fuel for continuation of the institutional trend. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — 0% hike priced. Risk: Leveraged funds begin profit-taking at the 0.7200 handle, triggering a positioning-led pullback.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Real Rate Backdrop
signals.text: GBP/USD is trading at 1.3595, supported by a 0.85% real policy rate that is among the most restrictive in the G10. The options market is pricing in a significant volatility risk premium, with 1M implied volatility at 11.0% vs a 30-day realized volatility of 5.8%. This +5.2% VRP suggests heavy institutional hedging demand ahead of the Jackson Hole symposium, where Chair Kevin Warsh is expected to speak. GBP positioning remains bullishly tilted with a COT LF net long of +46,070 (pctl 92), leaving the pair vulnerable to a 'buy the rumor, sell the fact' reaction if the Fed appears less dovish than expected. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; elevated vol premium makes premium-selling strategies attractive vs chasing the spot trend. Catalyst: Jackson Hole speech — Fed Chair Warsh. Risk: A sharp hawkish shift in Fed rhetoric triggers a broad USD rally, challenging the SMA200 at 1.3432.
